date-modified: last-modified

In this first week, we will cover what you can expect to learn from these exercises 
and how they differ from the main lecture. 
I will elaborate a bit on why I chose R for this course, what you can do
with it, and what has helped previous participants helped excelling in this 
course. Finally, I explain a bit what R is, how it relates to R Studio and LaTeX.

## 📚 Mandatory Reading

Work through the following resources on
[Method and Inquiry](https://euf-methodology-hub.netlify.app/), the methodology
hub of the Europa-Universität Flensburg:

- [Getting Started with R: Installing Everything You Need](https://euf-methodology-hub.netlify.app/resources/installing-r-and-rstudio) [@graebner2026-installing-r-and-rstudio]
- [Installing R Packages](https://euf-methodology-hub.netlify.app/resources/installing-r-packages) [@graebner2026-installing-r-packages]
  - 📥 The installation script referred to in this tutorial is specific to our
    course: download it here:
    [`install_packages_script.R`](install_packages_script.R). Save it in a
    directory of your choice, open it in R-Studio, adjust the first line to your
    operating system, and then run the whole script as explained in the tutorial.

In addition, read the course-specific page on
[using the exercise package](/content/material/UsingExercises.qmd).

## ✍️ Coursework

- Make sure you installed `R`, `R-Studio`, `Git` and all the required R packages
- If you have questions or problems, please post them in the Moodle forum
